label: cex-lhopital-converse
tail:
VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY: The limit as x→0 is a 0/0 form; f and g are differentiable on a deleted neighbourhood of 0, with g′=1≠0. The oscillator ψ is C¹ on ℝ, so f is differentiable for x≠0. As x→0, f(x)/g(x)=x ψ(1/x)→0, and f′(x)/g′(x)=2x ψ(1/x)−ψ′(1/x) has no limit because ψ′ takes the values 3 and −3 along sequences tending to infinity. Every boundary condition (non‑zero denominator, differentiability, existence of the required limits) is satisfied; no degenerate or empty case alters the argument.

SOURCES: All five cited dependencies were inspected. `ex-piecewise-polynomial-periodic-oscillator` supplies a bounded C¹ periodic function whose derivative attains ±3 in every period. `thm-chain-rule`, `thm-algebra-of-derivatives`, and `lem-derivative-of-a-power` correctly justify the computation of f′. `thm-lhopital-zero-over-zero` is cited only to note the forward implication. Each source supports its use.

CHECKED: The title, the public claim (converse of L’Hôpital), all three numbered steps (1.1, 1.2, 2.1), and the Remarks were examined. The witness is a valid counterexample: the hypotheses of the converse hold, yet the derivative quotient lacks a limit.
